# Vendored components

These source snapshots are committed with OpenLatch. Building either project
does not require the former HomeKey-ESP32 repository or recursive submodules.

| Component | Used by | Upstream commit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DigitalDoorKey | Indoor Home Key verification and credential provisioning | `28e5a13df5684ae6620402ca89cf106bde718845` |
| pn532_cxx | Outdoor PN532 frontend | `e1105d79c5628999371b8cc8aae37deb557e6ace` |
| pn532_hal | Outdoor PN532 ESP-IDF transport | `aeaacb67c8ba71d9b3907866ebe7a683eed8d26e` |
| loggable | PN532 logging support | `6a7c80d951c4833da0e527065eeb0bfc861bcabb` |

Each directory retains its upstream MIT license and copyright notices.
`manifest.json` records repository URLs, exact commits, selected files and their
SHA-256 hashes. Files were extracted from the committed upstream Git objects
without edits. The component-specific `.gitattributes` rules preserve their
original bytes and line endings without Git normalization.

DigitalDoorKey contains the HomeKey implementation and recursively referenced
headers needed by `indoor-controller`. Aliro/BLE implementations, examples, tests and
the upstream application are omitted. The Arduino adapter is generated by
`projects/indoor-controller/tools/prepare_homekey.py`; this subset is not a standalone
ESP-IDF component.

The other components retain their runtime sources, headers and ESP-IDF build
configuration. Upstream example/test directories are omitted; their optional
standalone host-test configurations are not used by OpenLatch. Outdoor logging
still uses the existing separately fetched **fmt 12.1.0** dependency. Indoor
cryptography and CBOR still use the pinned Arduino SDK and verified TinyCBOR
header described in the controller README.

For upgrades, replace the relevant snapshot, retain its license, update the
manifest, then run both projects' native tests and firmware builds.
